## How the work moves

::: {.site-lede}
The process is deliberately simple: clarify the problem, build the model and
software around it, translate results into business terms, then deploy with
monitoring, embedded engineering support, and team handoff.
:::
::::

::::: {.grid .site-card-grid}

::::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .site-card}
::: {.site-card__eyebrow}
Step 1
:::

### Problem Definition

We identify key pain points and opportunities, define success metrics aligned
with business KPIs, map existing processes and systems, and establish project
scope and timeline.
:::::

::::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .site-card}
::: {.site-card__eyebrow}
Step 2
:::

### Model Construction

We shape the data strategy, design the model architecture, build KPI-grounded
evals, train and validate, plan inference, and use post-training or RL
fine-tuning when feedback data makes it useful.
:::::

::::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .site-card}
::: {.site-card__eyebrow}
Step 3
:::

### Business Translation

Models matter only when they drive outcomes. We translate model metrics into
business KPIs, design experiments, and help teams capture downstream results.
:::::

::::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6 .site-card}
::: {.site-card__eyebrow}
Step 4
:::

### Deployment

We integrate systems, optimize inference, close the customer-data flywheel,
monitor performance, embed forward-deployed engineers when needed, and leave
teams with runbooks, dashboards, and ongoing support plans.
:::::

:::::
::::
